thread:
maria: Heads-up — staging metrics sidecar failing to mount secret volume after the TF change that updated the serviceaccount. Pod logs show permission denied reading /etc/metrics/creds. Anyone seen this after SA changes?

sam: can you paste 'kubectl -n staging get pod <pod> -o yaml' and the sa yaml? suspect automountServiceAccountToken=false or the RoleBinding subject got lost.

maria: pasted minimal outputs:

maria: ```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: metrics-writer
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/staging-metrics
automountServiceAccountToken: false
```

maria: Pod spec shows sidecar has volumeMount /etc/metrics from secret 'metrics-creds' which exists in namespace. Sidecar tries to read file, gets EACCES.

alex: if automountServiceAccountToken is false the projected token won't appear; but your sidecar reads a k8s Secret, not a projected token — are you using a job to create that secret that uses the SA? If the job can't talk to the API it won't create the secret. Check the job logs and SA RBAC.

maria: the secret is created by staging/metrics-secret-writer (a K8s job) that uses the metrics-writer SA. After the TF apply the job pod fails with 'Forbidden' when calling the API.

jen: likely TF recreated the ServiceAccount resource (new UID) and the existing RoleBinding references the old subject UID, so it's effectively empty. Run: `kubectl get rolebinding -n staging metrics-writer-bind -o yaml` and check subjects.

sam: also check TF state: did the module change how the SA is defined? I've seen templates that interpolate some secret name into the rolebinding subject and it becomes blank if the input changes.

maria: I ran describe and saw subjects: [] for the rolebinding. TF code shows rolebinding.subjects was built from a var that is now empty after a module ref change.

alex: quick remediation: patch the rolebinding to re-add the ServiceAccount subject (kubectl patch rolebinding ...) so the job can run and recreate the secret. Long-term: update TF module to reference the SA resource explicitly (not indirectly) or import the existing RBAC binding. Also consider lifecycle rules so TF doesn't orphan RBAC.

maria: patching now: `kubectl patch rolebinding metrics-writer-bind -n staging --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/subjects","value":[{"kind":"ServiceAccount","name":"metrics-writer","namespace":"staging"}]}]'`

infra-bot: noted: manual patch applied to rolebinding metrics-writer-bind in staging by maria at 2129457012

deploy-bot: retriggering job staging/metrics-secret-writer at 2129457020

maria: job logs show it hit the API and created secret metrics-creds. Pod got the secret mounted and reads succeeded.

sam: I'll open a small TF PR to make the module reference the SA resource and add an acceptance test. Also add a pre-apply check that ensures rolebinding.subjects won't be emptied by interpolation.

jen: FYI when using IRSA, SA resource churn is extra painful because RoleBindings/ClusterRoleBindings often store subjects by name/uid; prefer managing SA and its RBAC in the same module. Add a comment to the module docs.

maria: opened PR #842 with changes: reference serviceaccount resource, add acceptance test to the k8s pipeline, and a note about not interpolating secret names into subjects. Patch merged to staging.

infra-bot: job staging/metrics-secret-writer succeeded at 2129457085 (secret metrics-creds created)

maria: confirming sidecar pods now mount and can read /etc/metrics/creds. Closing the loop — thanks everyone :tada:

sam: thanks all, I'll follow up with a runbook entry about SA recreation + RBAC gotchas and add a terraform plan guard.

jen: added runbook note to infra-runbooks repo referencing PR #842 and the patch steps.

maria: will also add an alert to CI that flags rolebinding subjects being empty after applies.

alex: great. learning: avoid implicit interpolation for RBAC subjects, and when you have IRSA ensure TF and k8s RBAC lifecycle are aligned.
